channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens as surprise current account deficit weighs
item.description: USD/JPY advances 0.73% on Monday and trades around 158.95 at the time of writing.

item.title: The Canadian Dollar takes back two months in ten sessions
item.description: The Canadian Dollar trades at its strongest against the US Dollar since the second week of June, with the rate holding just above 1.3900 into the afternoon.

item.title: The Dow Jones Industrial Average kept what payrolls lost
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades near 54,000 on Monday, lower by a tenth of a percent inside a range of barely 200 points, the narrowest daily bar in weeks. Every price of the session sits inside Friday's range, and Friday's sat inside Thursday's.

item.title: British Pound climbs as Hormuz talks stall, US CPI in focus
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) advances during the North American session on Monday, up 0.2% as markets digest developments in the Middle East and await crucial inflation data in the United States (US). The GBP/USD pair trades at 1.3520 after bouncing off daily lows of 1.3483.

item.title: Emerging Markets: Selectivity key as Fed path clouds – HSBC
item.description: HSBC Asset Management notes that Emerging Market local-currency bonds have delivered strong returns over the past four years, supported by credible policies and attractive real yields, but year-to-date performance has softened as US Treasury yields rose and EM-US real rate differentials narrowed.

item.title: Denmark: Tax cuts keep inflation below the euro area – Nordea
item.description: Nordea economist Jan Størup Nielsen notes that Danish inflation eased slightly in July, with headline consumer prices up 1.7% year-over-year and core inflation steady at 2.3%.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Bearish pressure builds below 1.4000
item.description: USD/CAD trades on the back foot on Monday even as the US Dollar (USD) regains some ground after weakening last week following softer-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data. Attention now turns to Wednesday’s US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report.

item.title: Eurozone: Resilient data but growth risks weigh on Euro – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley notes Eurozone Q2 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) data surprised to the upside, suggesting resilience despite higher energy prices and supply disruptions.

item.title: Australian Dollar stays flat ahead of RBA rate decision
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) trades near the 0.7060 level against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, giving back a little ground after six straight weeks of gains.

item.title: Gold holds firm as Fed rate outlook, Middle East developments remain in focus
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) struggles to extend gains on Monday as buyers take a breather following last week’s sharp rally, with the broader market theme still centred on the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest-rate outlook and developments in the Middle East.

item.title: Euro holds ground against US Dollar amid Fed uncertainty ahead of US CPI
item.description: EUR/USD treads water on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) steadies following its post-NFP weakness, while Oil prices rise amid uncertainty over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1553, virtually unchanged on the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar jumps as Yen struggles with Japan’s fiscal woes
item.description: AUD/JPY rises 0.70% on Monday and trades around 112.25 at the time of writing. The pair benefits from broad weakness in the Japanese Yen (JPY), while the Australian Dollar (AUD) holds firm ahead of the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) monetary policy decision on Tuesday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Sideways growth and sticky inflation – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ US economists Oscar Munoz and Eli Nir expect US output growth to move sideways in 2026 as the lingering Oil shock and Iran-related risks keep the Federal Reserve on hold through year-end.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Faces risk of return to 160 against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole highlights that softer United States (US) data and a more dovish Fed outlook should, in theory, benefit the Japanese Yen (JPY) given its high rate sensitivity.

item.title: US Dollar: Positioning-driven softness ahead of CPI – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Wee Khoon Chong notes that the US Dollar (USD) has been the weakest G10 currency on iFlow metrics as markets scale back expectations for a September Fed hike.

item.title: Euro: Softer CPI may unlock 1.1600 against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that with key Eurozone data behind and European Central Bank (ECB) communication subdued, EUR/USD is now driven mainly by the United States (US) side.

item.title: British Pound rises against Japanese Yen as intervention impact fades
item.description: GBP/JPY edges higher on Monday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) underperforms across the G10 currency space, with structural headwinds limiting the impact of recent intervention. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 214.70, up 0.85% on the day.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Recovery against Euro may resume – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose notes that the Hungarian Forint (HUF) has only partially retraced its post-election gains and is expected to recover if global risk conditions stabilise, with EUR/HUF seen returning towards 350–355 in coming months.

item.title: Gold: CTA selling limits upside below $4,400 - TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ commodity strategists report that Gold is holding gains after weaker US jobs data reduced perceived Fed hike risks, but CTAs (Commodity Trading Advisors) are unwinding length.

item.title: WTI Oil jumps over 3% as Iran sets conditions for Strait of Hormuz reopening
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil rises 3.20% on Monday and trades around $78.80 at the time of writing. Oil prices retain strong daily gains, supported by uncertainty surrounding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and persistent tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Uptrend targets 0.7120 against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux notes AUD/USD has defended its 200-DMA and established a pattern of higher highs and higher lows, signalling a short-term uptrend.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Rate spread outlook favors JPY against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that JPY is underperforming as firmer Oil prices support USD/JPY, while the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) latest meeting minutes did little to shift rate expectations.

item.title: Copper: Weak China imports contrast with bullish positioning - ING
item.description: ING strategists Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson highlight that China’s latest trade data show continued weakness in copper imports, with unwrought volumes down 11.5% year-on-year and concentrate flows also softer.

item.title: US Dollar: Higher hurdle for sustained gains – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes that weaker US jobs data have not triggered a strong reaction in Dollar or rates, as markets await key Consumer Price Index (CPI) releases and another Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) before the September Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).

item.title: Euro: Modest upside bias against US Dollar as Fed repricing – Rabobank
item.description: Rabıobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses recent EUR/USD strength, noting it was mainly driven by a softer Dollar after weak United States (US) labour data reduced Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike expectations.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA policy pause maintained – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to leave the cash rate unchanged at 4.35%, noting that policy is already restrictive and that Australian activity, particularly housing, is slowing in response to earlier hikes.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ tightening risks support JPY – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Wee Khoon Chong highlights that long-end JGB yields are rising on inflation and fiscal concerns, with markets pricing a roughly 50% chance of a 25bp BoJ hike in September and a full hike by year-end.

item.title: Oil: Strait risk and cautious positioning – ING
item.description: ING analysts Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson note that Oil prices remain supported by uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran negotiations continue.

item.title: Silver tests $65: Why are buyers struggling to extend the rally?
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) struggles to extend its gains on Monday following last week’s strong breakout as traders assess the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest rate outlook amid risks on both sides of its dual mandate.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Rate hike odds slashed after soft inflation – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that Norwegian Krone (NOK) is trading mixed as firmer Oil offsets the drag from reduced Norges Bank tightening expectations.
